attributes.comment: Metadata attributes: #[Name(...)]. Distinct from the #{...} set literal.
attributes.name: meta.attribute.noeta

text-tier-blocks.comment: A text tier's `@<name> { … }` body is verbatim prose the compiler never lexes as code (text-tiers arc). std's `doc` is the built-in text tier; it is matched here — before #decorators — so the body's apostrophes/backticks/quotes can never open string scopes that bleed past the block. Brace counting mirrors the compiler lexer's matching_brace exactly: braces nest (the recursive #text-tier-brace-pair), and \{ / \} are literal braces with \\ a literal backslash (the escape pattern consumes them before any brace rule sees them). The CONTENT is scoped as a documentation *comment* (`comment.block.documentation.noeta`, `.comment.` also on nested prose brace pairs), so VS Code's bracket-pair colorization/matching skips prose `{`/`}`: it excludes brackets in comment/string tokens. The DELIMITER braces are deliberately NOT comment-scoped (`punctuation.section.tier.begin/end.noeta`): they are a real balanced pair, and — critically — VS Code's auto-indent evaluates its indentationRules against lines with brackets in comment/string tokens REMOVED, so a comment-scoped closing `}` becomes invisible to `decreaseIndentPattern` and Enter after the block would inherit the body's indentation (the multi-line `@doc { … }` indent bug). We deliberately do NOT inject `text.html.markdown` in the EDITOR: markdown's paragraph rule is greedy and swallows the closing `}` (scoping it `meta.paragraph.markdown`, standard-type Other), which re-introduces it as a counted bracket and drifts every following code brace's color. Instead #doc-markdown hand-rolls the accents doc prose actually uses (inline code, bold, italic, headings, bullets) with brace-free matches, so the muted comment base keeps markdown highlights without any rule that can swallow the closing brace; the docs *browser* still renders the body as full markdown. A third-party declared text tier (`@tier(x, text: "sql")`) ships its own injection grammar with a rule of this same shape (injectionSelector `L:source.noeta`) — that is the extension mechanism; this grammar stays static.

text-tier-escape.comment: The three text-body escapes: \{ \} \\ — literal braces/backslash, never counted. Matched ahead of the brace rules so an escaped closer cannot end the block.
text-tier-escape.name: constant.character.escape.noeta

text-tier-brace-pair.comment: A nested balanced brace pair inside a text body — recursion is how TextMate counts depth, so a `{snippet}` in prose does not close the block. The braces + content carry a documentation-comment scope so bracket colorization skips these prose braces too (see #text-tier-blocks).

doc-markdown.comment: Hand-rolled markdown accents for `@doc` prose — the subset doc comments actually use — in place of injecting `text.html.markdown` (whose greedy paragraph rule swallows the tier's closing `}`; see #text-tier-blocks). Every match here EXCLUDES unescaped braces, so no accent can ever consume a block delimiter, and none of these scopes contains `meta.embedded`, so the standard token type stays Comment (or String for raw spans) — invisible to bracket colorization. Scope names mirror markdown's own (markup.*), so themes color them exactly like real markdown.

patterns.comment: An ATX heading line: `# Title`. Stops at any brace so a one-line `@doc { # T }` still closes.
patterns.name: markup.heading.noeta

patterns.comment: A list bullet (the marker only, so the text keeps the comment base color).
An inline code span. `.string.` in the scope also excludes its content from bracket counting.
patterns.name: markup.inline.raw.string.noeta

patterns.comment: Underscore italic, word-bounded so snake_case identifiers in prose are never italicized.
patterns.name: markup.italic.noeta

decorators.comment: Directives and tier blocks: @derive(...), @role(...), @test, @bench(...), @debug. The decorator set {derive, attribute, role, semantic, packed} is fixed; every other @name is a tier (open set). @doc is carved out above as the built-in text tier.

patterns.name: string.quoted.single.noeta
patterns.comment: A single-quoted string is a RAW literal (lexer `RawStr`): it does NOT interpolate, and its only escapes are `\'` and `\\` — `${…}`, `{`, `$`, `\n` are all literal (ideal for regex/paths/JSON). So no `#interpolation` and no `#string-escapes` (which would honor `\u{…}`/`\x`/`\$` a raw string does not).

patterns.name: constant.character.escape.noeta
patterns.comment: The only two escapes a raw string honors.

patterns.name: string.quoted.template.noeta
patterns.comment: Backtick dedented-template string; supports the same ${...} holes.

patterns.name: constant.character.escape.interpolation.noeta
patterns.comment: An escaped interpolation opener: \${ is a literal dollar-brace.

interpolation.comment: A ${…} hole inside a string. The scope names deliberately mirror the JavaScript/TypeScript template-string convention (meta.template.expression + punctuation.definition.template-expression.begin/end) rather than an .interpolation.* naming of our own: every theme already ships two rules keyed on those names — one coloring the ${ } delimiters, and — critically — `meta.template.expression` which RESETS the region's foreground off the enclosing string color. Without that reset, the whole hole inherits string.quoted.*'s color and only tokens the theme styles more specifically (self, a call name) punch through, so bare identifiers and the delimiters read as string. The contentName meta.embedded.line.noeta flips the region's standard token type to Other so the code brackets inside a hole are counted/colorized as code, exactly as JS/TS do.
interpolation.name: meta.template.expression.noeta

patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.noeta
patterns.comment: Float, optionally with an exponent and an f32 suffix.
Function declaration: bind the name that follows `fn`.
Type declaration: bind the name that follows a type-introducing keyword.

storage-types.comment: Built-in primitive and standard container types.

types.comment: PascalCase identifiers are user-defined types (structs, classes, enums).
types.name: entity.name.type.noeta

function-call.comment: An identifier immediately followed by a call paren.
function-call.name: entity.name.function.call.noeta

patterns.name: keyword.operator.spread.noeta
patterns.comment: Must precede the range operator so `...` is not tokenized as `..` + `.`.
